title: Expiry and Forfeiture of Gift Cards & Store Credit Value
content:
Only Gift Cards & Store Credit types that expire ever expire. Return Store Credit and purchased gift cards (the Marlowe & Finch Gift Card and the Marlowe & Finch e-Gift Card) keep their value indefinitely and never carry fees.

## Terms of expiry

1. An expiring instrument stops working at the end of its expiry date, Eastern Time.
2. On the next day its remaining balance is forfeited in full.
3. An expiry date is never extended by an agent.
4. A forfeited balance is never restored, except through the reissue of a Marlowe Rewards Note under the refund rule.
5. An instrument that is locked, depleted or already closed on its expiry date does not move to expired.

## Day-by-day illustration (hypothetical Goodwill Credit with an expiry date of 30 June)

| Moment | Position |
|---|---|
| 11:50 pm Eastern Time on 30 June | Still working |
| After the end of 30 June, Eastern Time | Stopped working |
| 1 July | The remaining balance is forfeited in full |

## Status on the expiry date

| Status of the instrument on its expiry date | Moves to expired? |
|---|---|
| Active | Yes |
| Locked | No |
| Depleted | No |
| Closed | No |

## Basis questions

**Can an agent move the expiry date of a Bonus Gift Card by a week?** No. An expiry date is never extended by an agent.

**Is a forfeited Goodwill Credit balance ever put back?** No. The only forfeited value that returns is through the reissue of a Marlowe Rewards Note under the refund rule.

**Does a Return Store Credit lose value after a year without use?** No. Return Store Credit keeps its value indefinitely and never carries fees.
